comment: CAIRNWOLD's own art, layered over the shared bindings: the game merges this file onto art_bindings.json key by key, so the HUD, the icons, the effect sheets and the audio beds are the ones every region uses and only the world is this region's. A structure_prefixes key matches every placement whose id starts with it and picks one of its models per placement, which is how 90 birches share two trees. A building_walls key instead GATHERS every placement under it into one building, which is how Ashen Hollow builds a longhouse from four thin wall runs - so each cottage here has a key of its own.

cw_birch_.note: SIX BIRCHES, NOT TWO - AND THE TWO WERE THE SAME TREE. cw_birch_a and cw_birch_b both measured 5.08 x 5.15 x 9.54 m, so the ArtBindings hash was choosing between twins and the region's 90 birch placements read as one tree repeated. That is the owner's complaint measured rather than asserted. Six variants now span 8.06 to 11.46 m: c 8.06, d 8.93, a 9.54, b 10.54, e 10.78, f 11.46. GROWN BY _procgen_tree.py WITH DIFFERENT PARAMETERS, NOT JUST DIFFERENT SEEDS, because seeds alone were measured and were not enough - six seeds spanned 0.56 m of height (six percent), which is invisible at the distance the complaint lives at. --height, --crown-margin, --trunk-radius and --crown-lump now override the species table per run, which took the same six to a 3.40 m spread.

cw_pine_.note: SIX PINES, NOT TWO, and worse than the birch: cw_pine_a and _b both measured 7.61 x 7.38 x 13.37 m, and ALL SIX SEED-ONLY VARIANTS came out exactly 13.37 m tall - a spread of ZERO, because the species table pins the height and a seed only re-rolls the branches inside it. With --height overriding that table the six now span 11.82 to 15.54 m: c 11.82, d 12.80, a 13.37, b 14.03, e 14.50, f 15.54. 55 placements draw from them.

cw_wall_.note: ONLY THE 4.00 m PIECE, AND THAT IS A FIX. This declared both cw_wall_drystane_a (2.00 m) and _b (4.00 m), and ArtBindings picks a prefix's model with an FNV-1a hash of the PLACEMENT ID modulo the model count - so it was a coin flip per placement, and 22 of the region's 42 wall placements drew the 2.00 m piece. Every wall blocker is 2.6-2.8 m and consecutive blockers are spaced EXACTLY 4.00 m apart (2.8 + a 1.2 m gap = 4.00, and 2.6 + a 1.4 m gap = 4.00, checked on every pair). A 4.00 m piece centred on its blocker reaches 0.60 m past each end, so neighbouring pieces meet exactly and the wall is continuous. A 2.00 m piece reaches -0.40 m, SHORT of its own blocker, turning the 1.2 m gap into 2.00 m of daylight - isolated stubs with uniform gaps, which is what both blind reviews of this region described and what the drystone rebuild's own history records. _a is the pre-rebuild asset; _b was built at 4.00 m specifically to span this scheme. One model also makes the choice deterministic, so the wall can never disagree with itself again. ADDED fit 'tile': a drystone run is authored to butt end to end (a 4.00 m and a 2.00 m piece, 1.09 m high, both centred on X and Z, both ends flush). Without it the run draws ONE centred piece.

cw_hurdle.note: ADDED fit 'tile': the panel is 1.40 m of a woven run, authored to tile end to end.

cw_cart.note: 3.50 m overall, length on X, shafts toward -X (the frame _procgen_cart.py's header states).

cw_gate.note: 3.00 m five-bar gate, hinge end at the lowest x.

light.note: The light inside the lantern, at the candle's own head. A lantern post is a PROP, not a building, so the building loops in HollowView.BuildLighting (which iterate _bindings.Buildings) can never place this: it is placed by HollowView.ArtStructure's prop path, the same one that hangs a switch's glow shell on a prop's model.

cw_lantern.note: 2.80 m. 'material' drives the arrow-impact sound only; the post itself is timber (cw_timber_beam) carrying an iron lantern (cw_iron_dark), so 'wood' would be the truer sound - left as found. ADDED emitters + light: the thirteen posts were placed and drawn but never lit. A FLAME IS A PROP'S EFFECT AND THE OFFSETS ARE THE ASSET'S OWN METRES, so this entry's numbers are read out of the lantern post's own generator (_build/build_cairnwold_village.py, lantern_post()) and its meta's 0.905 x 2.80 x 0.35 m: the post's foot is the origin, the cross-arm runs to +X 0.62 at 2.72 m, the iron frame spans x 0.43-0.73 and y 2.10-2.58, and the candle inside it is a 0.16 m stub topping out at 2.28. So the flame sits at (0.58, 2.30) - the candle's head, inside the glass - and NOT at (0, 2.5): the model's bounds centre is 0.3025 m from the post, and Fitting re-centres a structure's model on those bounds, so a root-relative offset would put the flame a whole lantern-width beside the lantern it belongs to. HollowView.PropEffects therefore hangs the effects on the MODEL. Shadows are off on purpose: thirteen shadow-casting omnis in one village is a real cost and the reference pattern (src/Presentation/Art/VfxSheet.cs, the torch) uses none.

cw_granary.note: Raised store on six stone staddles; the floor platform is 1.02 m up and the walls are boarded timber.

interior_light.note: The hearth under the lodge's own chimney, at the model's local x +3.2, z +1.15 - the chimney building_spec() put there. A range of 17 m because the hall is 18 m long and a lodge lit only at one end reads as a barn from outside; warm and low, the same family as the cottages' lamps.

cw_longhouse_.note: THE COMMUNAL LODGE, generated by tools/asset_pipeline/_procgen_building.py from the region's own cw_longhouse_* wall runs, so its walls coincide with the region's blockers (the build checks that on a 5 cm grid and the provenance records the agreement). It is built from CAIRNWOLD's materials - cw_wet_stone_wall for the plinth, the infill and the chimney, cw_timber_beam for every timber member and the floor, cw_slate_roof for the roof - and not from the shared procedural ashlar set, because every house in this village is photographic rubble stone and regular machine-perfect courses on the largest building in the region would read as a kit piece.

structures_by_visual_option.note: ADDED, and INERT for two reasons, both outside this region's files. (1) ArtBindings skips an option key that VisualOptions.All does not contain, and there is no 'cairnwold_roofs' key in src/Presentation/VisualOptions.cs - registering one is a code change, not a content one. (2) cw_roof_slate and cw_roof_thatch are WHOLE roofs, not panels: cw_house_timber_a already carries a roof node of its own, so a slate village means hiding that node and standing cw_roof_slate in its place, which lands on the same wall plate because both are authored to the same 8.72 x 6.78 m eaves rectangle, ridge 6.50 m, origin at the footprint centre on the ground. Until both are settled these two files are bound to nothing and the game will never draw them - recorded here so that is a known state rather than a surprise.
